Definition: A single score combining how available, how fast, and how defect-free a piece of equipment or line is running, compared to its full potential.
Similar to OEE but measured across a whole operation rather than one machine -- combining availability, speed, and quality into one score.
On average, how long a piece of equipment runs between breakdowns. Higher means more reliable equipment.

Also known as: Mean Time To Repair; Mean Time To Resolve
Definition: On average, how long it takes to fix something once it breaks or an issue is raised.
The pace production needs to run at to match customer demand -- if you make one unit every Takt Time, you exactly keep up with orders.
How long it actually takes to complete one unit of work, start to finish.
Time equipment or a process was stopped and not producing.
The share of available time or capacity that was actually put to productive use.
A philosophy of making small, continuous improvements to a process over time.
A production approach that aims to make or receive materials just as they're needed, rather than holding large amounts of inventory.

Also known as: Work In Progress; Work In Process
Definition: Units that have started production but aren't finished yet.
The amount of output produced for a given amount of input, such as units made per labour hour.
How much useful output is achieved compared with the resources or time used.

Also known as: Labor Efficiency; Labour Utilization; Labor Utilization
Definition: The share of available working hours that produce useful output.
The amount of product or work completed in a given period of time.
The quantity of goods or work produced in a period.
How much of the available production capacity is actually being used.
The share of planned time that a machine or system was ready to run. In OEE it is one of the three parts, with performance and quality.
How fast a machine ran compared with its best possible speed while it was running. It is one of the three parts of OEE.

Also known as: First Time Quality; Good Parts Rate
Definition: The share of parts made that were good the first time. It is one of the three parts of OEE.
Time when a machine is stopped on purpose, for example for maintenance, changeovers or breaks.

Also known as: Breakdown Time; Unscheduled Downtime; Unplanned Stops
Definition: Time when a machine is stopped because of faults or other events nobody planned.
The time taken to switch a machine or line from making one product to making the next.

Also known as: Units Produced; Production Quantity; Production Output
Definition: The number of units made in a period. It is the basic measure of how much a plant produced.

Also known as: Schedule Adherence; Plan Attainment; Schedule Attainment
Definition: How closely actual production matched the production plan, shown as a percentage of what was planned.
How much was produced compared with what the equipment and people should have produced in the same time.

Also known as: Unit Cost; Cost per Unit; Manufacturing Cost per Unit
Definition: The total cost of production divided by the number of units made.

Also known as: Output per Labour Hour; Units per Labour Hour
Definition: The amount produced for each hour of labour used.
The labour cost divided by the number of units made.
The share of available machine time that was spent producing.
How much of the available capacity of equipment or other assets was actually used.

Also known as: Installed Capacity; Rated Capacity; Maximum Capacity
Definition: The most output that a machine, line or plant can produce in a period under normal conditions.
The capacity that has not yet been taken up by orders, so new work can be accepted.
The step in a process that limits how much the whole process can produce, because everything else has to wait for it.
How evenly the work is shared between stations on a production line, so that none is idle while another is overloaded.
A measure of how well a process keeps its output inside the allowed limits. A higher figure means fewer parts are out of tolerance.
The share of total lead time that is spent on work that adds value for the customer, with the rest being waiting and handling.
The time spent on activities that change the product in a way the customer will pay for.
The time spent on activities that do not add value for the customer, such as waiting, moving or checking.
Anything in a process that uses time, money or material but does not add value for the customer.
A way of working that aims to remove waste and keep only the steps that add value for the customer.
The habit of making many small, regular improvements to how work is done, rather than waiting for big changes.

Also known as: Employee Suggestions; Suggestions Implemented; Ideas Submitted
Definition: The number of improvement ideas put forward by staff, often shown together with how many were put into practice.

Also known as: PM Compliance; Planned Maintenance Percentage; PPM
Definition: The share of scheduled preventive maintenance jobs that were carried out on time.
Repair work done after something has broken, as opposed to work planned in advance.
The money spent on keeping equipment working, including labour, spare parts and outside contractors.

Also known as: Maintenance Work Orders Closed; Closed Work Orders
Definition: The number of maintenance jobs that were finished in a period.
The number of maintenance jobs that have been requested but are not yet finished.
The average time a part or machine runs before it fails, used for items that are replaced rather than repaired.
The share of spare part requests that could be met straight from stock.

Also known as: Energy Use; Power Consumption; Electricity Consumption
Definition: The amount of energy used in a period, for example in kilowatt hours.

Also known as: Energy Intensity; Energy Consumption per Unit
Definition: The energy used for each unit produced. It allows fair comparison between busy and quiet periods.
The amount of water used in a period. It is tracked to find ways to save water and cost.
The amount of waste produced by operations in a period, often split into recycled and landfilled.
The share of waste that was recycled or reused rather than thrown away.

Also known as: CO2 Emissions; Carbon Footprint; Greenhouse Gas Emissions
Definition: The amount of carbon dioxide, or its equivalent in other greenhouse gases, released by the business's activities.
A measure of how well labour is used, combining how available people are, how fast they work and how good their output is.
How well equipment is used over all the hours in a period, whether or not they were planned for production.

Also known as: Plan vs Actual; Output vs Plan
Definition: A comparison of what was planned to be produced with what was actually produced.

Also known as: Order Cycle Time; Order to Delivery Time
Definition: The time from when a customer places an order to when it is delivered.
The difference between the planned and the actual completion of work, shown in time or as a percentage.

Also known as: On-Time Project Delivery; Projects Delivered On Time
Definition: The share of projects that were finished on or before their planned date.
The number of requests for work or service received by an operations team in a period.
The share of cases where the agreed process was followed from start to finish.
The hours of labour spent fixing work that was not right the first time.
Time when people or machines are paid for or available but doing nothing because there is no work or something is holding them up.
